company.about: Northwind Labs is a small software company building Slotly, a B2B scheduling SaaS for clinics and service teams, with engineers and AI coding agents working side by side.

events.text: Good morning, Northwind! ☀️ Big week ahead: **Slotly 2.4** ships on Friday (recurring availability + Google Calendar sync v2). Planning starts at 10:00 → https://meet.northwind.test/planning
Sprint board is live: https://slotly.example/board/sprint-24. Please add your estimates before 10:00 so we don't burn half the meeting on it.
Facilities: fire drill today at 14:00 (meet at the car park), and yes, we are out of oat milk. A delivery is coming around lunch 🥛
Quick one: who keeps taking the tall monitor stand from the 3rd floor? 👀
Not me, I'm a laptop-on-a-stack-of-books person.
Did anyone watch the city marathon yesterday? A man in a banana costume beat my personal best. Again.
Same banana as last year? Asking for the honour of the whole chat.
Heads up: two on-site interviews for the Senior Product Designer role this week (Tue 14:00 and Thu 11:00). Invites are in your calendars. Please be kind and punctual 🙏
Support inbox is calm this morning. Touching wood and saying nothing else.
Please don't say anything else 😄

Backend scope for 2.4:
- **Recurring availability** API (Boris)
- **Calendar sync v2** webhook handler (Dmitri)
- **Rate limiting** on `/public/slots` (Victor)
Shout early if an estimate looks wrong.
Taking recurrence. I'll let Claude Code · API draft the migration and the model, and I'll review everything before it touches staging.
For the sync webhook: Google can deliver the same notification twice. Do we dedupe by `X-Goog-Message-Number` or store our own idempotency key?
Our own key, stored for 24h. Google's header isn't guaranteed to be stable across channel renewals.
For rate limiting: token bucket in Redis or in-process? In-process won't survive multiple pods behind the load balancer.
Redis, we already run it. I'll drop the staging URL in the vault. Keep keys namespaced like `rl:{tenant}:{route}`.
Reading the `availability_windows` model and its 14 call sites. Plan: add a nullable `recurrence_rule` (RFC 5545 RRULE subset) and a `RecurrenceExpander` service.

events.question: Migration `add_recurrence_rule` adds one nullable column, no backfill. Apply it on staging now?

events.text: Migration applied on staging in 340 ms. Model and expander are on branch `feat/recurrence`, 31 unit tests green.
Looks clean. One nit: the expander must cap at 366 occurrences per query, otherwise a weekly rule with no end date is a memory bomb.

events.title: Recurring availability: schema, model, expander
events.summary: Added nullable `recurrence_rule` to availability_windows and a RecurrenceExpander that turns RRULE subsets (daily/weekly, until/count) into concrete windows. API layer and DST edge cases are still open.
done: Model validation for the RRULE subset

events.text: FYI the analytics export reads `availability_windows` directly. Tell me before the column shape changes so I can update the pipeline.
Only one nullable column was added, your export is untouched.
QA plan for recurrence is on the board. I need staging data with DST edge cases (Europe/Berlin spring-forward week). Boris, can you seed it?
Will do after lunch.
Product question: is the 366 cap visible to customers? I'd want a clear message if somebody hits it.
Planning notes: Backend committed to the three items above and nothing else. Please push back on scope creep, including from me.
Maintenance note: I'm upgrading the staging Postgres minor version at 18:00, expect about 5 minutes of downtime.

Web scope: recurring availability editor (Frank), booking page performance (Wendy), and the settings redesign from Leo's latest Figma. Codex is scaffolding the editor so Frank can focus on interaction details.
Scaffolding `RecurrenceEditor`: weekday chips, time range rows, end date picker. Reusing the existing `FormField` and `TimeRange` primitives.
Great, I'll pair with it this afternoon. Wendy, do you have a Lighthouse baseline for the booking page?
Yes: LCP 3.4s on throttled mobile, mostly the calendar widget bundle. Target is under 2.5s. https://slotly.example/perf/booking-baseline
Accessibility reminder: the weekday chips need real buttons with `aria-pressed`, not clickable divs. I'll test with a screen reader on Wednesday.
CDN cache rules change tonight so hashed assets get immutable caching. If you see stale JS tomorrow, tell me.
Mobile scope: offline booking queue (Hugo on iOS, Xavier on Android) and push notifications for rescheduling. Release candidate Thursday noon, store review Friday.
Auditing the sync layer for the offline queue. Two places assume the network is always there: `BookingRepository.create` and `ReminderScheduler`.
iOS: I'll use a persistent queue in Core Data. My concern is conflict resolution when the slot got taken while the phone was offline.
Same on Android with Room. Proposal: the server answers 409 plus the next free slots, and the app shows them as suggestions.
That matches the product intent. Max 3 suggestions, same day first.
Offline banner copy and state designs are in the mobile frame. Keep it calm, no red unless the booking actually failed.
Q4 roadmap draft. Comments welcome until Wednesday.
Looks good. Where does SSO land? Enterprise prospects keep asking.
Second half of Q4, depends on what Thursday's demo reveals.
Research update: we ran 6 interviews last week. The top pain is not scheduling itself, it's rescheduling when someone cancels. Full summary tomorrow.
Very useful. Mia, can you add three direct customer quotes? They help a lot in investor updates.
Sales confirms: rescheduling is the number one objection we hear. Please keep it in the roadmap talking points.
Week targets: 3 demos, 2 proposals sent, Brightfield decision by month end. Let's go 💪
Brightfield Clinics demo is Wednesday 15:00. I need a stable staging environment by then.
Brightfield Clinics demo is **Thursday 15:00** (not Wednesday, sorry!). I need a stable staging environment by Wednesday evening.
Quinn, can you share the objection handling doc? I'm calling the clinic list at 11.
Last week's outbound numbers: 412 emails, 38 replies, 9 meetings.
Customer Success note: 3 clinics asked whether recurring availability will support split shifts. I'm adding them to the feedback doc.
Support tip: customers keep emailing the old booking page URL. I added a redirect FAQ: https://slotly.example/help/old-booking-links

That is almost the whole connection limit. Which service is opening them?

Oh no. It's the rate limiter. `createClient()` runs on every request and early returns never close it. My fault, sorry everyone.

events.title: Incident analysis: Redis connection leak in rate limiter
events.summary: Root cause: `createClient()` called per request in the rate limit middleware; early returns skipped `quit()`. Connections reached the server limit within 14 minutes of the peak. Rollback to 2.3.6 recovered service.
done: Confirmed connection count back to baseline
next: Load test the limiter on staging
